I've always been sceptical of 'gene centered' selection for the simple reason that no gene ever comes in a package all by itself. It is always 'packaged' with thousands of others. If gene 'a' confers a certain fitness on its possessors this advantage is diluted practically to infinitely small by the fitnesses (or not) of the other genes, some of which will be 'fitter' and some less so. If the article fairly represents Dawkins' present views then he hasn't changed his opinion in decades.
